prompt: Which property increases down group 1 from lithium to caesium?
markscheme: **C.** Each element down the group has an extra occupied shell, so the outer electron is further from the nucleus. Ionization energy, electronegativity and melting point all decrease.

prompt: Which species has the smallest radius?
markscheme: **D.** All have 18 electrons; Ca²⁺ has the most protons (20) pulling them in.

prompt: What is the oxidation state of vanadium in NH₄VO₃?
Which element has a lower first ionisation energy than the element immediately before it in period 3?
markscheme: **C.** S loses an electron from a doubly occupied 3p orbital; repulsion makes it easier to remove than P’s.

prompt:

**(c)** Outline why aluminium oxide is described as amphoteric, giving one equation. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH}$ ✓; $\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ ✓

**(b)** NaOH solution pH > 7 (≈ 13–14) and H₂SO₄ solution pH < 7 (≈ 1) ✓

prompt:
A solution of [Ni(H₂O)₆]²⁺ is green.

**(a)** Write the electron configuration of Ni²⁺ (Z = 28). **[1]**

**(b)** Explain why the complex is coloured. **[3]**

**(c)** Suggest why a solution containing [Zn(H₂O)₆]²⁺ is colourless. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** [Ar] 3d⁸ ✓

**(b)** The water ligands split the 3d orbitals into two sets of different energy ✓; electrons absorb visible light of energy matching the gap and are promoted to the higher set ✓; the complementary colour of the absorbed light (red/purple absorbed) is transmitted/observed ✓

**(c)** Zn²⁺ is 3d¹⁰: the d sublevel is full, so no d–d transitions are possible ✓
